module: lua-MessagePack (François Perrad, MIT license, base version 0.5.1, adapted by BeamNG in 2022): MessagePack binary serialization. This version uses LuaJIT's string.buffer and a shared work buffer; it can also serialize vec3 and quat (cdata). A modder uses it to encode/decode Lua tables into compact binary strings (network exchange, files).
usage:
local mp = require('libs/lua-MessagePack/MessagePack')
local bin = mp.pack({a = 1, b = {1, 2, 3}})
local data = mp.unpack(bin)
notes: All numbers are written as doubles (0xCB), never as compact integers. When reading, MessagePack integers are converted to Lua numbers.
A Lua string is written as binary (bin8/16/32), not as MessagePack str; when reading, str and bin both become Lua strings.
Default array mode: 'without_hole' (called at the end of the file): a table is written as an array if its keys are 1..n without holes, otherwise as a map. Change with set_array.
vec3 are written as a map {x,y,z} and quat as a map {x,y,z,w}; any other cdata is written as the string '?'.
packWorkBuffer and packPrefixWorkBuffer return the shared internal buffer (bufTmp): its content is overwritten at the next pack call; consume it immediately.
Unhandled types (function, thread) raise the error "pack '<type>' is unimplemented".
Extension types (ext): build_ext returns nil by default, so ext values read become nil unless build_ext is replaced.

pack.desc: Serializes a Lua value into a MessagePack string.

data.desc: nil, boolean, number, string, table, vec3, quat, string.buffer.

packWorkBuffer.desc: Like pack, but returns the shared work buffer without converting it to a string (avoids a copy).

returns.desc: Internal string.buffer, reused on each call.

packPrefix.desc: Serializes data preceded by the string prefix.

prefix.desc: Bytes to write before the data.

packPrefixWorkBuffer.desc: Like packPrefix, but returns the shared work buffer.

set_array.desc: Chooses how Lua tables are serialized: 'without_hole' (array if consecutive indices without holes, otherwise map), 'with_hole' (array up to the max index if all keys are positive numbers), 'always_as_map' (always a map). Any other value raises an error.

unpack.desc: Deserializes a string containing exactly one MessagePack value. Raises a 'missing bytes' error if it is truncated and 'extra bytes' if bytes remain.

unpack_cursor.desc: Decodes the next value from a cursor {s, i, j, underflow}, advancing c.i.

unpacker.desc: Returns an iterator that successively decodes several values: from a string (returns the position and the value) or from a function supplying chunks of data (returns true and the value).

src.desc: String, or function returning the next chunk (or nil).

build_ext.desc: Hook called for each extension value read; the default implementation returns nil. Replace it to decode your extension types.
